messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall (raj) — automated canary health check failing for `payments-service` rollout in us-west-2. Error rate spiked to 18% and 502/504 on write paths. Root TS: 1779998888

alice: starting canary rollout for release v2026.02.15 at 12:03 UTC. migration `add_idx_order_ref` applied to canary-db only. low-risk, small alter. rolling 10% canary.

raj: on it. hitting the channel. can you paste the deploy id / migration id?

alice: deploy id: deploy-20260215-2043. migration id: m_20260215_01_add_idx_order_ref. logs show ALTER TABLE stuck at 12:05 UTC.

maria: seeing long-running transaction holding lock on orders: pid=32518, age=00:27:12. query: `ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN order_ref text;`

maria: ps aux snippet:
```
postgres  32518  0.5  1.2 234567 12345 ?    S    12:05  0:00 postgres: replica conn 10.0.2.12 m_ix
postgres  32521  0.0  0.8 123456  7890 ?    S    12:05  0:00 ALTER TABLE orders ...
```

maria: and lock table output:
```
pid  |  locktype | relation | mode  | granted
32518 | relation  | orders   | AccessExclusiveLock | true
32490 | txnid     |         | ExclusiveLock       | false
```

sophie: customers hitting 502s on checkout. paging from support. initial impact ~15% of traffic to us-west checkout.

pm-jordan: which customers? any paying customers impacted? need a customer-impact blurb for comms.

alice: early telemetry says small subset of accounts on canary edge nodes — mostly internal QA + a few customers on canary routing groups (beta). no major enterprise traffic yet. will confirm.

kevin: suggest immediate mitigation: flip feature flag to stop canary traffic and then abort migration on canary nodes. if flag can't be flipped fast enough, we may need to kill the session holding the lock.

marco: +1 to flag. How do we flip? ops-bot, can you perform a kill-switch?

ops-bot: @here received request: set feature flag `payments_canary_v2026_02` -> off for us-west-2. Running...

ops-bot: done. flag set to off (scope: region=us-west-2, rollout=canary). Traffic should drain in ~30s.

alice: traffic draining. but migration still stuck because session persists.

raj: can we find who owns pid 32518? db-admin, can you run `pg_terminate_backend(32518)` if safe? Need confirmation of read replicas / downstream effects.

db-admin: 32518 is the migration worker started by `deploy-20260215-2043`. It is not replication streaming. Terminating will roll back the ALTER TABLE partially — but it should be safe. There is a small chance of causing a short spike in retries.

maria: if we terminate, tables will revert to previous state. but we must ensure migrations on other DBs won't pick up an inconsistent partial state. current state: only canary-db attempted it. Primary and replicas unchanged.

kevin: i'm leaning to terminate to restore customer traffic. Sophie, confirm immediate customer risk vs rollback time.

sophie: we need checkout working now. please terminate. support is sending customers a temporary status update.

alice: ok going to terminate the session now. will also add a hold in deploy system to block further rollout.

alice: running: `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(32518);`

maria: ack seeing termination. migration rolled back on canary-db. AccessExclusiveLock released.

ops-bot: deploy guard applied: `canary-rollout` paused for deploy-20260215-2043.

kevin: good. verify traffic recovery stats.

raj: checking metrics — error rate back down to baseline within 45s. 502s dropped to <1%.

pm-jordan: thanks. need brief incident note: cause = migration on canary hit long-running lock due to open session, prevented traffic drain; mitigation = feature-flag kill + terminate migration session + pause rollout. impact = brief customer 502s to small canary cohort, no paid customers impacted beyond minor errors; RCA pending.

marco: question: how did a session stay open that long? was the migration written with transactional DDL that blocked?

maria: looks like a background process held an idle-in-transaction connection (old Tx) — blocked the DDL. devs should avoid long idle tx during schema changes.

alice: followups: 1) add deploy guard to block migrations on canary unless session checks pass 2) require pre-check script that ensures no idle transactions older than X 3) run the migration manually on canary again after freeze window and add retry/backoff.

raj: handing off to next oncall. my shift ends in 45m. @sophie you'll take lead for immediate follow-up, and i'll draft the incident stub.

sophie: taking it. I've created a ticket and assigned to `eng-ml` and `db-ops`: ITR-2026-312.

alice: created rollback branch `hotfix/20260215/canary-migration-safety` with guard code. PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4218

ops-bot: deploy bot: rollback request accepted. queued rollback for canary nodes only.

kevin: one more check — ensure migration not auto-applied to primary during subsequent rollouts. lock the migration registry.

db-admin: migration registry set to `paused` for that change id.

incident-bot: incident opened: INC-2026-0223. Severity: S2 (partial customer impact). Pager escalations stopped.

pm-jordan: good job all. we'll schedule a blameless postmortem. please add notes on the runbook gap (preflight checks) and the feature-flag play.

raj: handoff complete — next oncall is sophie. I log notes in the incident doc. over to you. :thumbsup:

sophie: ack. I will own follow-up and coordinate rollout safe path. closing this thread for active paging.

alice: thanks team.

kevin: closing comms: support update sent to customers at 12:12 UTC.

ops-bot: thread archived to incidents channel as INC-2026-0223.
